newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo planning more liberal foreign trade regime.
newsitem.headline: Yugo planning more liberal foreign trade regime.

text.p: Yugoslavia plans to further liberalise its foreign trade regime, a senior government official said on Thursday.
"The government aims to further liberalise the country's foreign trade," the Yugoslav trade minister Djordje Siradovic told a gathering of Serbian businessmen.
To help the export drive and show commitment to truly liberal trade, the government will soon launch a new customs regime with Macedonia, he said.
"This would give us more access to the market of Macedonia but also of other countries," Siradovic said, adding that Yugoslav companies should not be afraid of competition.
According to Siradovic, the share of trade regulated by quotas has already been cut from 25 to 11 percent.

"Abandoning quotas now would mean a further opening of our market. But the government is still considering new, more subtle mechanisms, to retain a degree of protection for domestic producers," Siradovic said.
"Protection from imports can in part be achieved with customs tariffs," he said.
The minister blamed local banks for not being generous in financing new industrial production after U.N. sanctions were suspended in November.

He said banks were also guilty of failing to provide finance for export programmes and major construction projects abroad by Yugoslav companies, adding that the government was working on a new export credit insurance scheme.
"Faced with a lack of foreign investment, we must do something about export credit insurance and besides, foreigners expect some changes in our system," he said.
Siradovic also said his ministry would establish a new commission to tackle monopolies. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
